tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Choreographic Intention & Communication

questions.question: Q: What is choreographic intention?
questions.correctAnswer: Choreographic intention is the purpose or message the choreographer wants to communicate through the dance — it guides every creative decision.

questions.question: Q: How do motifs help communicate choreographic intention?
questions.correctAnswer: Motifs are key movement phrases that embody the core idea. By developing and varying motifs throughout the dance, the choreographer reinforces the intention so the audience recognises and understands it.

questions.question: Q: Why might an audience interpret a dance differently from the choreographer's intention?
questions.correctAnswer: Each audience member brings their own experiences and perspectives, so they may understand the movement in a different way. Multiple interpretations are valid and enrich the dance.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Choreographic Intention & Communication

questions.question: Q: How do dynamics contribute to communicating mood in a dance?
questions.correctAnswer: Dynamics such as sudden, sharp movements can create a tense or aggressive mood, while sustained, flowing movements can create a calm or lyrical mood — the quality of movement directly affects atmosphere.

questions.question: Q: Explain why a choreographer must ensure the intention is clear from the movement itself.
questions.correctAnswer: If the intention can only be understood through a title or programme note, the movement has not effectively communicated. A successful dance conveys its meaning through the choreography so the audience can engage with it directly.
